paragraphs.text: SALT BASIN
GENESIS
Program, Repository, Computational Mapping & Immersive Enterprise Experience Specification
From scientific foundation → governed enterprise emergence → playable operating reality
Version 1.0  |  2 August 2026  |  Program Owner: Martha Elizabeth Salter
Salt Basin Holdings  |  Proprietary & Confidential
Document Control
Purpose

This specification defines how a multidisciplinary team completes, governs, implements, and renders Salt Basin Genesis as one coherent system. It is the authoritative handoff for repository population, scientific-to-enterprise translation, configurable business equations, evidence-backed decisions, temporal simulation, and the immersive enterprise-management experience.
Normative language

“Must” denotes a required control. “Should” denotes a recommended design with an allowed, documented exception. “May” denotes an optional capability. Scientific analogy never supersedes law, accounting guidance, contracts, company policy, security, consent, agent scope, or user entitlement.

1. Executive Definition

Salt Basin Genesis is the governed creation and runtime framework that links a canonical scientific knowledge foundation to a separately governed enterprise operating model. It compiles validated structural mechanisms—composition, identity, interaction, state, transformation, invariance, emergence, observation and retained history—into enterprise patterns. Those patterns are then bound to organization-specific objects, journeys, policies, equations, evidence and authority.

The output is not a themed dashboard. It is an auditable enterprise operating reality in which every visible form, movement, constraint and outcome can be traced backward to configured business meaning, source evidence, policy versions and—where applicable—the scientific mechanism that shaped the computational behavior.
2. Fundamental Goal and Non-Goals
2.1 Fundamental goal

Enable an enterprise to configure and operate flexible, multi-party journeys that behave reproducibly under explicit rules; preserve meaning and evidence through change; show why an action is allowed, blocked or escalated; and project the governed state into an explorable world without sacrificing accounting controls, legal authority, security or historical truth.
2.2 What Genesis is not
It is not a literal claim that a database field is a proton, a customer is an atom, or an enterprise is a mineral.
It is not a system that lets a scientific metaphor authorize a contract, journal entry, payment, entitlement or disclosure.
It is not a replacement for source-system permissions when sensitive data must remain distributed.
It is not a static ontology, a single linear lifecycle, or a visualization detached from computational records.
It is not a game whose mechanics can invent business outcomes without evidence and provenance.
3. Governed Program Model

The three workbooks form one governed program but have different authority. They must not be delegated as three independent files to be “finished.” Work is delegated in bounded definition packages, reviewed by domain owners, and released into controlled masters.
3.1 Integration authority

A single Integration Architecture Council arbitrates cross-repository identity, namespaces, schemas, mapping acceptance and release readiness. The Program Owner retains final product authority. Scientific accuracy, enterprise meaning, financial control, security and visualization each have named veto authority within their defined domain.
3.2 Record lifecycle

All governed records follow: Proposed → Researched → Reviewed → Approved → Implemented → Validated → Superseded/Retired. A record’s status is independent from the release containing it. Approved records are changed through a versioned change request, never silent editing.
4. Repository System of Record
5. Canonical Scientific Foundation

The scientific foundation remains an evidence-backed, versioned registry of scientific definitions. The 17-level navigational spine is a discovery view, not a claim that all of nature is one universally accepted linear taxonomy. Typed relationships represent composition, instantiation, transformation, classification and emergence without encoding known category errors.
5.1 Required completion domains
Quantum fields, elementary particles, antiparticles and composite particles
Atomic nuclei, nuclides, isotopes, atoms, elements, ions and polyatomic species
Bonding, interactions, molecular structures and transformations
Crystal systems, lattices, unit cells, symmetry, minerals and rocks
Geological structures, stratigraphy, sedimentary and evaporite basins
Regional geological systems, ecosystems and Earth systems
Properties, equations, laws, measurement methods, instruments, uncertainty and sources
Coverage denominators, combination spaces, sufficiency gates and unresolved scientific questions
5.2 Completion acceptance

Every canonical scientific concept must have a stable ID, definition, type, applicable scope, evidence status and source assertions. Equations must link atomically to variables, units, assumptions and boundary conditions. Scientific render glyphs must be labeled as abstract visualization states unless they are direct measurements or accepted structural models.
6. Enterprise Canonical Foundation

The enterprise foundation defines reusable business meaning across operating model, legal structure, multi-party relationships, offerings, commercial journeys, financial events, controls, evidence, attribution, risk and value. It is a typed polyhierarchy: one object may participate simultaneously in identity, contract, accounting, customer, entitlement and evidence contexts.
7. Translation Compiler and Mapping Layer

The mapping layer is a compiler, not a synonym table. It extracts a reusable mechanism from science, proposes an enterprise structural equivalent, binds it in a specific context, tests evidence and counterexamples, and only then permits implementation as an equation, predicate, transition rule or render behavior.
7.1 Twelve mapping gates
7.2 Mapping contract

Each accepted mapping must contain: Mapping ID; scientific source mechanism; abstract formal pattern; enterprise target; binding context; cardinality and grain; identity rule; state variables; executable expression or predicate; evidence requirements; counterexamples; authority sources; confidence; validation status; effective version; reviewer and decision record.
7.3 Mapping classifications
Exact formal correspondence — same mathematical or logical structure within stated boundaries.
Structural analogy — useful recurrent pattern with documented differences.
Context-dependent analogy — valid only for a named object, stage, policy or grain.
Visualization-only analogy — permissible render metaphor with no decision authority.
Rejected mapping — recorded to prevent rediscovery or misuse.
8. Parallel Equation and KPI Registries

Genesis requires two independent equation systems plus an optional pattern linkage. Business equations may reuse a formal mechanism, but they cannot overwrite a scientific equation or gain authority simply because a scientific analogy exists.
8.1 Variable binding

A configured KPI never embeds unresolved field names inside an opaque formula. Each variable links to a semantic property, grain, source event, aggregation rule, unit/currency, time window, missing-data behavior, reconciliation requirement and access policy. Formula evaluation stores the exact variable bindings and input evidence used.
8.2 Example
9. Configuration Journey

A business is mapped into Genesis through a controlled configuration journey, not a one-time data import. Configuration produces a versioned operating model that can be simulated, tested, approved and activated.
Establish organization namespace, legal boundary, environments and authoritative sources.
Define parties, structures, roles, offerings, commitments and entitlements.
Map current and target capabilities, processes, journeys, rods, stages, branches and merge rules.
Register business definitions, policies, equations, KPIs, accounting rules, controls and thresholds.
Bind source objects, fields, events and evidence to canonical semantics.
Validate identity, grain, units, cardinality, state and temporal rules.
Configure agents, user entitlements, consent, exposure, action permissions and approval boundaries.
Compile predicates and state transitions; test valid, invalid, exception and rollback scenarios.
Generate render bindings and world projections from governed properties.
Run parallel simulation; reconcile outputs; approve effective-dated activation.
9.1 Configuration artifacts

Every configuration release produces a manifest, schema bindings, policy bundle, equation bundle, journey graph, transition matrix, agent/security policy set, evidence requirements, render profile, migration plan, validation report and rollback reference.
10. Decision and Control Runtime

The runtime evaluates whether a proposed movement is permitted and explainable. It does not infer permission from a visual state. A transition request is evaluated against effective authority, required evidence, reconciliation status, security, consent, agent scope, user entitlement and exception pathways.
11. Temporal, Evidence and Lineage Architecture

Every atom, definition, mapping, equation, rod, branch, stage, action, observation, cache and decision is temporal. Genesis must answer what was known, what rule was effective, what evidence existed, what changed, who or which agent acted, and how the current state emerged.
11.1 Evidence chain

Evidence links thesis or intent → definition → measurement → source events → reconciliation → attribution → financial outcome → exit defense. Confidence is computed from evidence quality, completeness, lineage, reconciliation, temporal coverage, ownership and counterexample strength; it is not a manually selected decoration.
11.2 Branching and merging

Every journey rod and branch has a bounded agent. When a branch merges, the active branch agent closes and a Historical Lineage Agent preserves the complete branch context, evidence, decisions and contribution to the parent journey. No merge may erase divergent history.
12. Agent-Centric Security and Distributed Data

Security is agent-centric as well as user-centric. Each agent has scoped source systems, data-access policy, allowed transformations, memory-retention rules, exposure rules and action permissions. The interacting user’s organization, role, profile slice, consent and read/write entitlements further constrain what the agent may reveal, query, stage or commit.

When source environments prohibit centralization, DataBasin operates as a governed aggregation, normalization and semantic projection layer. Scoped source-side queries and calculations execute under each source’s native permissions. Only authorized outputs, metadata, evidence references and permitted aggregates enter the Genesis layer.
13. Simulation and Computational Model

The simulation engine operates on the same governed objects, equations, policies and events as the production runtime but inside isolated scenario branches. It supports state propagation, counterfactuals, stress tests, forecasts, capacity constraints, resource flows, causal hypotheses and uncertainty.
13.1 Required computational primitives
Typed entities and compositions
Directed and undirected interactions
State machines and eligible transitions
Temporal event streams and effective-dated definitions
Equations, predicates, constraints and optimization objectives
Units, dimensions, currencies, conversions and rounding policies
Probabilistic variables, uncertainty and confidence
Branch, merge, replay and comparison
Reconciliation and invariant checking
Deterministic projection outputs for every committed simulation state
13.2 Emergence rule

A higher-order enterprise representation may emerge only from explicitly configured lower-level composition and validated transformations. The mineral representation is therefore a projection of governed data composition, maturity, evidence and process history—not a new fact source. Its geometry and material state must be reproducible from the underlying records.
14. Immersive Enterprise World and Render Grammar

The experience should feel like a rigorous management simulation—closer to SimCity or RollerCoaster Tycoon in agency and systemic consequence—while retaining enterprise-grade traceability. Users configure, observe, diagnose, simulate and act within a persistent world that can zoom from enterprise orbit to one evidence-bearing event.
14.1 Deterministic render grammar
14.2 Seven-channel meaning

“7D” is an experience shorthand, not a claim of seven physical spatial dimensions. The initial scientific rendering channels are 3D position, time, compositional/structural state, velocity/change rate, lineage and uncertainty/confidence. Each channel is named, versioned and reversible to data.
14.3 User capabilities
Build or configure the enterprise and its multi-party ecosystem.
Watch journeys, evidence chains, capital flows and financial events form and move.
Inspect fractures, bottlenecks, weak evidence and control failures.
Rewind, replay and compare historical or simulated branches.
Change an authorized configuration and preview propagated consequences before commitment.
Ask bounded agents why a state exists, why an action is blocked and what evidence would remediate it.
Move between orbit, rod, molecule/object, atom/data element and source-evidence views without losing context.
15. Initial Playable Vertical Slice

The first vertical slice proves the full chain from configuration through authoritative transaction, financial reconciliation, KPI movement, evidence and immersive projection. Recommended scope: Prospect → Executed Contract → Invoice → Cash → Reconciliation → ARR / EBITDA Evidence → Thesis Impact.
15.1 Explicit exclusions

The first slice does not attempt full portfolio coverage, every scientific domain, unrestricted generative world-building, production payment initiation, autonomous contract execution, or universal causal attribution. Those follow only after the slice reconciles end to end.
16. Team, Workstreams and Authority
17. Repository Population Playbook
17.1 Teams do not edit masters directly

Contributors work in controlled intake packages. Stable IDs are reserved centrally. Approved records are integrated through release automation with duplicate, orphan, schema, source, coverage and policy checks.
17.2 Definition package workflow
Scope the bounded domain, denominator and dependencies.
Reserve candidate IDs and assign owner, researcher and reviewer.
Research authoritative sources and capture atomic assertions.
Draft canonical definitions, properties, relationships, equations and examples.
Record counterexamples, open questions and rejected mappings.
Run automated structural checks and domain review.
Approve or return with decision notes.
Integrate into release candidate and execute cross-repository tests.
Validate in runtime and projection where applicable.
Publish release, coverage change and supersession lineage.
17.3 Minimum completion criteria
No semicolon-delimited foreign keys where junction records are required.
No duplicate canonical definition under multiple names without synonym control.
Every foreign key resolves; every approved assertion resolves to a source.
Every equation has variables, units/dimensions, assumptions, boundary conditions and applicability.
Every mapping has counterexamples and authority boundaries.
Every organization configuration is namespaced, versioned and effective-dated.
Every runtime transition has valid, invalid, unknown, exception and replay tests.
Every render binding is deterministic and reversible to underlying data.
18. Work Packages and Backlog
19. Quality, Testing and Acceptance
19.1 Repository tests
Primary-key uniqueness and namespace validity
Foreign-key integrity and permitted cardinality
Canonical-definition duplication and synonym collision
Source/assertion traceability
Equation-variable-unit completeness and dimensional consistency
Coverage denominator type: exact, versioned, estimated, lower-bounded, open or unbounded
Status, effective dates, supersession and change-request lineage
19.2 Runtime tests
Authorized and unauthorized read/write paths
Allowed, blocked, unknown, exception and expired transition states
Policy-version and evidence-time replay
Branch, merge, correction and rollback behavior
Reconciliation invariants and rounding/currency rules
Missing, late, conflicting and low-confidence evidence
Agent scope and user-entitlement intersection
Deterministic simulation seeds where reproducibility is required
19.3 Experience tests
Same governed state produces same render under the same render-profile version.
Every visible object and motion resolves to underlying IDs and calculations.
Security changes visibility without corrupting shared lineage.
Users can distinguish measured state, calculated state, forecast, hypothesis and visual metaphor.
Zoom, rewind, replay and comparison preserve context.
No decorative visual state is mistaken for a financial, legal or scientific fact.

Approval

This specification becomes the program baseline when approved by the Program Owner and acknowledged by the named domain authorities. Subsequent changes must identify affected repositories, mappings, configurations, runtime behavior, tests, visual bindings and migration requirements.
